label: Task modifier text
summary: Text about the modifiers a council task gives, for the task key you pass.
details: Going by its name and three localization lines that call a same-named function on a councillor with a council task key in quotes (for example 'task_foreign_affairs') to describe the task's effect. Those lines may use another type, so this is a hint. It returns text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The council task key, in single quotes.
fields.values: a council task key such as 'task_foreign_affairs'

label: Modifier text
summary: A text describing how the character is affected by one modifier, named by its key.
details: Takes the modifier's key as text. Vanilla uses it in the army supply breakdown for the commander, with `'supply_capacity_mult'` and `'supply_capacity_add'`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a modifier key in quotes, like `'supply_capacity_add'`

label: Monthly legitimacy
summary: The character's monthly legitimacy, as text.
details: The game's main screen (hud.gui) shows it as a text field. Going by its name it is the amount per month; the game says nothing more.

label: Monthly legitimacy tooltip
summary: A data object about the character's monthly legitimacy, which the main screen hands to a GUI element as its data.
details: The main screen (hud.gui) uses it as a datacontext. Going by its name it feeds a tooltip. Its return type is not registered in the game's documentation.

label: Mother
summary: The character's mother, as a character you can chain further functions onto.
details: Vanilla chains it in the event window's child naming texts, for example to check whether the mother is the local player or to show her short name.

label: Mother or father
summary: The word 'mother' or 'father', matching the character.
details: Vanilla uses it in nicknames ('the [Mother/Father] of Spain', 'the Blood-[Mother/Father]') and as a verb ('has not been able to [mother/father] a child'). It is not the character's mother's father.

label: Movement power from merit
summary: The movement power the character gets from their merit, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the merit text after the movement power concept, formatted with a sign.

label: Councillors title
summary: Text for the title of this character's councillors, taking one argument.
details: Judged from the name alone: vanilla never uses it and the game does not say what the argument is.

label: Name
summary: The character's name.
details: Vanilla uses it all over its texts, for messages such as "[Character] is not a player". Its sibling GetNameNoTooltip gives the name without the hover tooltip, which suggests this form comes with one.

label: Name with nickname
summary: The character's name together with their nickname.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla uses it once, for the defeated side of a historic battle on a battle point of interest ('Defeated: [name]'). The exact form is not shown.

label: Name with nickname, plain
summary: The character's name together with their nickname, without the hover tooltip.
details: Going by its name and the NoTooltip pattern of the other name functions. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nickname, regnal, plain
summary: The character's name with nickname and regnal number, without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone (regnal means the ruler number, as in Henry II). Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed name or me
summary: The character's name with nickname, or a word for the player instead when the character is the player.
details: Going by its name and by the similar GetNameOrMe, whose vanilla lines choose between 'are' and 'is' depending on whether the character is the player. Vanilla has no use of this one.

label: Nicknamed name or me, plain
summary: Like the name with nickname or me, but without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed or me, regnal, plain
summary: The name with nickname and regnal number, or a word for the player, without the tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed or me, regnal
summary: The name with nickname and regnal number, or a word for the player when the character is the player.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed possessive name
summary: The character's name with nickname in possessive form (the "'s" form).
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed possessive, plain
summary: The possessive form of the name with nickname, without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed possessive, regnal, plain
summary: The possessive form of the name with nickname and regnal number, without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed possessive or my
summary: The possessive form of the name with nickname, or a word like "my" when the character is the player.
details: Going by its name and by the similar GetNamePossessiveOrMy, which vanilla texts use. Vanilla has no use of this form.

label: Nicknamed possessive or my, plain
summary: Like the possessive name with nickname or "my", but without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed or my, regnal, plain
summary: Possessive name with nickname and regnal number, or "my", without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed possessive or my, regnal
summary: Possessive name with nickname and regnal number, or "my" when the character is the player.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Nicknamed possessive, regnal
summary: The possessive form of the name with nickname and regnal number.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Name with nickname, regnal
summary: The character's name with nickname and regnal number.
details: Judged from the name alone (regnal means the ruler number, as in Henry II). Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Name, no tooltip
summary: The character's name as plain text, without the hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it a lot, for example in the texts for releasing a tributary and for an accolade requirement.

label: Name, regnal, no tooltip
summary: The character's name with regnal number, without the hover tooltip.
details: Going by its name. The one same-named line in vanilla is a coronation event text that follows another type, so it is a hint only.

label: Name or me
summary: The character's name, or a word for the player instead when the character is the player.
details: Going by its name and same-named vanilla texts that choose between 'are' and 'is' depending on whether the character is the player. Those lines may use another type.

label: Name or me, no tooltip
summary: The character's name, or a word for the player, without the hover tooltip.
details: Going by its name and two hold court event lines that use the same name on a vassal. The game documents nothing more.

label: Name or me, regnal, plain
summary: The name with regnal number, or a word for the player, without the tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Name or me, regnal
summary: The name with regnal number, or a word for the player when the character is the player.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Possessive name
summary: The character's name in the possessive form, like 'Alfred's'.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla puts it before the thing owned: '[name's] travel will be paused', 'We do not consider [name's] faith to be hostile'.

label: Possessive name, no tooltip
summary: The character's name in possessive form, without the hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in tournament result texts and in a tournament GUI tooltip about progress towards victory.

label: Possessive name, regnal, plain
summary: The possessive name with regnal number, without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Possessive name or my
summary: The character's name in the possessive form, or 'my' when the character is the player, going by its name.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla uses it in rite texts, capitalised: '[name's] rite is ...', '[name's] is head of rite'. That it gives 'my' for the player is read from the name only.

label: Possessive name or my, plain
summary: Like the possessive name or "my", but without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Possessive or my, regnal, plain
summary: Possessive name with regnal number, or "my", without the hover tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Possessive name or my, regnal
summary: Possessive name with regnal number, or "my" when it is the player.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Possessive name, regnal
summary: The possessive name with regnal number.
details: Going by its name. Two same-named lines in vanilla, a house feud text and a court event text, write it after a saved character.

label: Name, regnal
summary: The character's name with regnal number (the ruler number, as in Henry II).
details: The regnal meaning comes from the name. Same-named lines appear in a tournament event text and a dynasty banner text; they are a hint only.

label: Appointment cooldown date
summary: The date until which the character cannot be appointed to a title.
details: Vanilla shows it in tooltips like "Cannot be appointed until ...", followed by GetString on the date. "New" in the name is not explained by the game.

label: Nickname
summary: The character's nickname, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the texts of the effect that removes a nickname ('Loses the nickname ...').

label: Nickname, no tooltip
summary: The character's nickname as plain text, without the hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in the shared tooltip layout, formatted with |U.

label: Accolade slots
summary: The number of accolade slots the character has.
details: Vanilla shows it as the limit in "Accolades: x/y" and checks it is above 0 in the knights window.

label: Accolade slots breakdown
summary: The text listing where the character's accolade slots come from.
details: Vanilla puts it under the accolade limit in a tooltip.

label: Accolade count
summary: The number of accolades the character currently has.
details: Vanilla shows it as the first number in "Accolades: x/y".

label: Free accolade slots
summary: The number of accolade slots the character has left.
details: Going by its name and knights window lines where it is compared with a slot index. Those lines call it on the character of the military view, so the type is not certain.

label: Pending court events
summary: The number of court events waiting for the character since they last attended court.
details: Vanilla shows it in the royal court status and the main screen checks that it is above 0.

label: Titles from theocratic lease
summary: The number of titles the character holds through a theocratic lease.
details: Vanilla shows it in the character window as the count of temples held under the faith's lease contract.

label: Vassals toward limit
summary: The number of the character's vassals that count towards the vassal limit.
details: Vanilla compares it with the vassal limit in the realm window and shows an element when it is higher.

label: Number of buildings
summary: The number of buildings the character has.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number in the ledger.

label: Controlled holy sites
summary: The number of holy sites the character controls.
details: Same-named vanilla lines use it on the player and on a faith, never on a character directly, so this is a hint.

label: Kills known to
summary: The number of the character's kills that the given character knows about.
details: Vanilla passes the player and shows the number in the ledger. That the kills are ones the character committed is read from the name, not from the game.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who must know about the kills.

label: Number of prisoners
summary: The number of prisoners the character holds.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger and hides the field when it is zero.

label: Obedience breakdown
summary: The breakdown of the character's obedience, as a data object for a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of an interaction and of the shared tooltip layout.

label: Obedience target
summary: The character this character owes obedience to, going by the name.
details: Vanilla shows its short name in the shared tooltip and checks that it is valid. Who counts as the target is not stated.

label: Obedience threshold breakdown
summary: The breakdown of the obedience threshold, as a data object for a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as data in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Obedience tooltip text
summary: The description text for the character's obedience tooltip.
details: Vanilla puts it as text in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Obscured text
summary: A text for the character used in the shared tooltip layout.
details: Going by its name, it is a text for a hidden or obscured case; the single vanilla use only puts it as a text field in the shared tooltip. The game documents nothing more.

label: Opinion breakdown text
summary: The text listing how the opinion between this character and the given character is made up.
details: Vanilla passes the liege or the suzerain of the shown character in the character window. Which side's opinion is meant is not shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, such as the liege

label: Opinion heading text
summary: The heading text over the opinion breakdown between the character and the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the liege or the suzerain, in the same places as the breakdown text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, such as the liege

label: Opinion of
summary: The character's opinion of the given character, as a number.
details: Vanilla passes the player to show "opinion of me" and can show the sign. Opinion can be negative.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the opinion is about.

label: Opinion color
summary: A color (four numbers) for the character's opinion of the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it as a font tint in the outliner and character window, next to opinion numbers. The game does not say which colors it gives.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the opinion is about.

label: Organization
summary: A group the character belongs to, as a data object.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a character window part. What kind of group it is, the game does not say; this rests on the name.

label: Birth name
summary: The character's first name as given at birth.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Birth name" in a tooltip.

label: Overlord
summary: The character's overlord, as a character you can chain further functions onto.
details: Vanilla uses it in realm window texts to check whether the overlord is the local player and to show their name.

label: Perk points
summary: The number of perk points the character has for the given lifestyle.
details: Vanilla passes the lifestyle and shows it in the lifestyle window as perks left to unlock.

label: Perk points used
summary: The number of perk points the character has used in the given lifestyle.
details: Vanilla shows it as a count of unlocked perks out of the lifestyle's total, and checks it is above 0.

label: Tenet change cooldown end
summary: When the cooldown on changing personal tenets ends for the character.
details: Vanilla shows it in the personal beliefs window in "You may change your personal tenets again in ...". Whether it is a date or time left is not shown.

label: Personal tenet gain text
summary: Text for gaining a personal tenet, taking one argument.
details: Judged from the name alone: vanilla never uses it and the game does not say what the argument is.

label: Personal tenet loss text
summary: Text for losing a personal tenet, taking one argument.
details: Judged from the name alone: vanilla never uses it and the game does not say what the argument is.

label: Personal tenet slots
summary: The number of personal tenet slots the character has.
details: Going by its name and its whole-number return type. Vanilla has no use of it; its breakdown sibling is used in the personal beliefs window.

label: Tenet slots breakdown
summary: The text listing where the character's personal tenet slots come from.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the personal beliefs window, on the character shown there.

label: Personal tenets
summary: The list of the character's personal tenets.
details: Going by its name. The one vanilla line with this name is a data list of the personal beliefs window itself, another type, so it is a hint.

label: Piety
summary: The character's current piety.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number in the character, intrigue and church windows.

label: Piety balance
summary: The character's piety balance, shown with a sign.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger and checks whether it is at least 1. Going by the name it is the net piety gain or loss per period; the game does not say the period. It can be negative.

label: Piety level
summary: The character's piety level, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla divides it by 40 in the ledger to set a transparency. That the top level is about 40 is a guess from this.

label: Piety level icon
summary: The icon image for the character's piety level.
details: Vanilla uses it as an image in the character, intrigue and ledger windows.

label: Piety progress to next level
summary: How far the character has come towards their next piety level.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a progress bar in the ledger.

label: Piety tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the character's piety, including the balance.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the character, intrigue and ledger windows.

label: Place in succession
summary: The character's place in line to inherit the given title.
details: Same-named vanilla texts write it like "you are 2nd in line" and pass a title. Those lines use the name on a saved character; the type is not shown.

label: Playable character
summary: The playable ruler this character stands for.
details: Vanilla passes it to the multiplayer lobby's control, can-control and tooltip calls. Going by the name, it is the ruler to take control of.

label: Playable frame
summary: A frame number for the playable marker of the character, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name and its sibling GetPlayableFrameTooltip, which portraits use. Vanilla has no use of this one.

label: Playable frame tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the playable marker on a character portrait.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip in the shared portraits file.

label: Dread effect icon frame
summary: The icon frame number for the effect the player's dread has on this character.
details: Vanilla uses it as an icon frame in the shared portraits file, next to a tooltip function.

label: Dread effect tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the effect the player's dread has on this character.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip on portraits.

label: Dynasty relation frame
summary: The icon frame number for how the character relates to the player's dynasty.
details: Vanilla uses it as an icon frame in the portraits file, and shows the icon only when the number is below 9.

label: Dynasty relation tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for how the character relates to the player's dynasty.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip on portraits.

label: Guest description
summary: A text about the character as a guest of the player.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Player heir
summary: The character's heir in the sense of the player's succession, as a character you can chain further functions onto.
details: Going by its name. Same-named vanilla lines call it on the character of a selected playable in the multiplayer lobby and inside a destiny value call; what exactly counts as the player heir is not stated.

label: Interaction accept effects
summary: The text describing what happens when the given interaction is accepted, as the player would use it on this character.
details: Vanilla uses it once, with a treasury transfer interaction key, in a tooltip. That the effects are those of acceptance comes from the name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

label: Interaction name
summary: The display name of the given interaction as the player would use it on this character.
details: Vanilla uses it a great deal as button text, with keys like 'recruit_guest_interaction'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

label: Interaction reject effects
summary: The text describing what happens when the given interaction is rejected.
details: Going by its name and its accept sibling. Vanilla has no use of it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

label: Interaction tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the given interaction as the player would use it on this character.
details: Vanilla uses it widely as the tooltip of buttons in the main screen and windows.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

summary: The text listing why the given interaction cannot be used on this character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

summary: The tooltip of the given interaction when it targets an artifact.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

label: Interaction tooltip, character
summary: The tooltip of the given interaction when it targets another character.

label: Interaction tooltip, secret
summary: The tooltip of the given interaction when it targets a secret.
details: Vanilla uses it in the intrigue window with the blackmail interaction.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

label: Interaction name, title
summary: The display name of the given interaction when it targets a title.
details: Going by its name and its tooltip sibling. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Interaction tooltip, title
summary: The tooltip of the given interaction when it targets a title.
details: Vanilla uses it in the administrative vassal details with candidacy interactions.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The interaction key, in single quotes.

summary: The description of what kind of heir the player's succession gives.

label: Player heir type icon
summary: The icon for the kind of heir the player's succession gives.

label: Player heir type name
summary: The name of the kind of heir the player's succession gives.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip headed "Player Heir type".

label: Portrait animation tooltip
summary: The text about the animation the character's portrait is playing, for a given widget.
details: Vanilla passes the widget itself in the barber shop and the shared tooltip layout. The meaning comes from the name.

label: Portrait frame number
summary: The frame of the portrait border of the character.

label: Powerful vassal frame
summary: The icon frame number that marks the character as a powerful vassal.
details: Vanilla uses it as a frame in the outliner, the tournament and the portraits file.

label: Powerful vassal tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the powerful vassal marker.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the outliner, the tournament and portraits.

label: Prestige
summary: The character's current prestige.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number in the character, confederation and ledger windows.

label: Prestige balance
summary: The character's prestige balance, shown with a sign.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger and checks whether it is at least 1. Going by the name it is the net prestige gain or loss per period; the game does not say the period. It can be negative.

label: Prestige level
summary: The character's prestige level, as a whole number.

label: Prestige level icon
summary: The icon image for the character's prestige level.

label: Prestige progress to next level
summary: How far the character has come towards their next prestige level.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a progress bar in the ledger.

label: Prestige tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the character's prestige, including the balance.

label: Prisoners
summary: The list of characters the character holds as prisoners.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of the ledger.

label: Promoted legend

label: Realm heir type icon

fields.text: The character the relation is measured against.

summary: The character's religious superior.
details: The same name is used in the character window as data on the shown character; going by the name, it is who stands above them in their faith.

label: Religious top superior
summary: The character's highest religious superior.
details: Going by its name and its GetReligiousSuperior sibling. Vanilla has no use of it.

label: Revoke reasons
summary: The text listing the reasons the title may be revoked from the character.
details: Going by its name and interaction texts about being allowed to revoke a title; the lines there use the name after a saved character.

label: Rite
summary: The character's rite, as an object you can chain further functions onto.
details: Vanilla uses it often (hundreds of uses of the name), for example in texts about adopting a personal tenet, where it is passed to the tenet name function. What a rite is here, the game does not say.

label: Royal court blockers
summary: The text listing what blocks the royal court for the character.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the main screen. The meaning comes from the name.

label: Scripted value breakdown
summary: The breakdown of a scripted value for the character, as a data object for a tooltip.
details: Judged from the name alone. Vanilla has no use of it; the argument is presumably the scripted value.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; probably the scripted value.

label: Seal coat of arms
summary: The coat of arms used on the character's seal.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of the shared coat of arms layout.

label: Secret faith
summary: The faith the character secretly follows.
details: Returns a faith. Vanilla takes its name in secret and interaction texts: 'Practices [faith] in secret', '... practices Crypto-[faith]'.

label: Sexuality
summary: The character's sexual orientation, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the "Sexual Orientation" tooltip of the character window.

label: Sexuality frame
summary: The icon frame number for the character's sexual orientation.
details: Vanilla uses it as an icon frame in the character window and the shared tooltip layout.
